chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated, who said: Abdullah ibn Musa ibn Harun al-Mufti narrated, who said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Arzami narrated, who said: Al-Ma'la ibn Hilal narrated, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas

He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) say: God, Blessed and Exalted, gave me five things and gave Ali five things: He gave me the essence of speech and gave Ali the essence of knowledge; He made me a Prophet and made him my Trustee; He gave me Al-Kawthar and gave him Al-Salsabil; He gave me Revelation and gave him Inspiration; He took me on the Night Journey to Him and opened for him the doors of the heavens and the veils, so that he saw what I saw. The hadith is long; we have taken from it what is needed, and I have recorded it in its entirety in the book of Al-Mi'raj.

key_terms.السَّلْسَبِيل: A source of flowing, sweet water in Paradise
key_terms.الْكَوْثَر: A river or pool in Paradise granted to the Prophet
key_terms.الْوَصِيّ: The Trustee or Successor designated by the Prophet
key_terms.جَوَامِعَ الْعِلْمِ: The essence or comprehensive core of knowledge
key_terms.جَوَامِعَ الْكَلِمِ: The essence or comprehensive core of speech/rhetoric

ai.seo_question: What are the five things God gave to the Prophet Muhammad and the five things He gave to Imam Ali according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal* establishes a theological symmetry between the Prophet and Imam Ali, positioning Ali’s spiritual station as the complementary counterpart to the Prophet’s prophetic mission. By granting Ali 'Jawami' al-Ilm' (comprehensive knowledge) and 'Wasiyyah' (successorship), the text underscores the Shia belief that divine guidance continues through the Imamate after the cessation of Revelation. The parallel gifts of Al-Kawthar and Al-Salsabil further link the Prophet’s universal bounty with the Imam’s specific role as the source of spiritual sustenance for the faithful.
